```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
# R code here is ASCII only (HTML entities for special characters), so the page renders the same in any locale
A <- "docs/assets/ctwas_scz_filter_reads10nc"
jp <- fread(file.path(A, "joint_params.tsv")); jg <- fread(file.path(A, "joint_gene_pips.tsv")); jc <- fread(file.path(A, "joint_convergence.tsv"))
jtr <- fread(file.path(A, "joint_traits.tsv")); cmp <- fread(file.path(A, "compare_gene_pips.tsv")); ws <- fread(file.path(A, "weights_steps.tsv"))
TPS <- c("0hr", "1hr", "6hr")
tpl <- function(x) sub("hr", " hr", x)
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
fp <- function(x) vapply(x, function(z) if (is.na(z)) "NA" else format(signif(z, 2)), "")
cell <- function(x) fifelse(is.na(x), "&ndash;", sprintf("%.2f", x))
j8 <- jg[gene_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]
old8 <- cmp[gene_pip_isolaser >= 0.8, gene_name]
gp <- function(t) jp[group == paste0(t, "|splicing")]
w0 <- ws[step == "QTL set filter_reads10nc"]; wt <- ws[step == "top QTL per part"]
```

We ran cTWAS on the schizophrenia (SCZ) GWAS with our isoLASER associations as
splicing QTLs, using **isoLASER + filter**: isoLASER's `cis` label plus
|ΔPSI| &ge; 0.05. This page repeats the joint run of the
[earlier cTWAS page](isolaser_ctwas_scz.html), which used the `cis` label alone,
with these weights. cTWAS asks whether the splicing QTLs explain more GWAS
heritability than SNPs in general (**enrichment**), and which genes' splicing is
likely causal (**PIP**, the posterior inclusion probability).

**Short answer.**

- **Enrichment:** `log_enrichment` is `r sprintf("%.2f", gp("0hr")$log_enrichment)` at 0 hr and
  `r sprintf("%.2f", gp("6hr")$log_enrichment)` at 6 hr. At 1 hr the prior goes to about 0:
  in the joint run the 1 hr traits explain nothing beyond the 0 and 6 hr traits
  ([why](#parameters)).
- **prop_heritability** of the splicing groups: `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * sum(jp[group != "SNP", prop_heritability]))`
  together, most of it at 6 hr.
- **Genes:** `r length(j8)` genes reach `combined_pip` 0.8: `r paste(j8, collapse=", ")`.
  With the `cis` label alone there were `r length(old8)`. The filter removes
  `r paste(setdiff(old8, j8), collapse=", ")` and adds `r paste(setdiff(j8, old8), collapse=", ")`.
- **The filter removes the high-coverage `cis` calls:** above about 2,370 reads isoLASER's
  `cis` cutoff falls below 0, so nearly every association there is labelled `cis`
  with ΔPSI near 0. On the earlier page ACTB, COX6C and RPL13 rested on such parts;
  none of them is in a fine-mapped region now.

# How the runs were set up

- **GWAS:** PGC schizophrenia, `ieu-b-5102` (N = 127,906), z-scores harmonized to
  the UK Biobank (UKB) LD reference, from the earlier multigroup cTWAS project.
- **Molecular traits** (our definition): one trait per tested exonic part. A part
  is included when one of its associations has isoLASER's `cis` label, computed
  from the panel-heterozygous donors with at least 10 reads each, and
  |ΔPSI| &ge; 0.05 (isoLASER + filter; no FDR cutoff). That is
  `r paste(fmt(w0$associations), collapse=" / ")` associations at 0 / 1 / 6 hr.
- **QTL and weight:** each trait has one SNP, the part's variant with the smallest
  permutation p (ties: largest \|ΔPSI\|) among its associations that pass the
  filter, single-base variants in the UKB reference that are not
  strand-ambiguous. The weight is ΔPSI (ALT minus REF inclusion) with ALT as the
  effect allele. With one SNP per trait, only the weight's sign matters. This
  gives `r paste(fmt(wt$parts), collapse=" / ")` traits, of which cTWAS keeps those whose
  SNP is in the GWAS (`group_size` below).
- **Mapping table:** each trait (exonic part) maps to the gene the part belongs
  to. It is written with the weights and used for gene-level PIPs.
- **One run:** the three timepoints as separate groups in one run
  ([how](#all-timepoints-jointly)), with the same settings as the earlier page.
- **Settings:** UKB b38 LD, no thinning, one prior variance shared by all groups
  (`shared_all`), up to 5 signals per region (L = 5), at least 100 traits per
  group. Regions are fine-mapped when their non-SNP PIP is at least 0.5.
- **Not done yet:** merging regions and checking LD mismatch.

## What the tables and figures show

**Parameters**, the output of `summarize_param()`:

- **group_size:** splicing traits that reach cTWAS after matching to the GWAS and the LD reference.
- **group_prior:** the estimated prior probability that a trait (splicing) or a
  variant (SNP) is causal.
- **group_prior_var:** the prior variance of a causal effect, shared by all groups (`shared_all`).
- **log_enrichment:** the log of a splicing group's prior over the SNP prior, with
  its standard error; **enrichment_pval** is its p-value.
- **group_pve:** the proportion of SCZ variance explained by the group:
  group_size &times; group_prior &times; group_prior_var / GWAS N. **total_pve**
  sums all groups.
- **prop_heritability:** a group's group_pve over total_pve, the slices of the
  pie chart.

**Convergence**, from `make_convergence_plots()`: the estimates at each iteration
of the parameter estimation. Proportion causal (&pi;) is `group_prior`, effect
size (&sigma;<sup>2</sup>) is `group_prior_var`, enrichment
(&pi;<sub>G</sub>/&pi;<sub>S</sub>, not on the log scale), and PVE. Flat lines
at the end mean the estimates have settled.

**Gene-level PIPs:** `combined_pip` combines a gene's exonic parts with
`combine_gene_pips()` (`method = "combine_cs"`, `filter_cs = FALSE`: all parts,
whether or not they are in a credible set). It sums the parts' `susie_pip`
within each credible set and combines credible sets as
1 &minus; &prod;(1 &minus; sum). Parts that share a top SNP are identical
predictors and split their PIP, so a gene's `combined_pip` can be high when none
of its parts is.

# All timepoints jointly

**How the joint run works** (Xin's suggestion; read-based only): one run with the
three timepoints as separate groups, `0hr|splicing`, `1hr|splicing` and
`6hr|splicing`, each with that timepoint's weights and its own `group_prior`;
`group_prior_var` is shared. A part tested at several timepoints enters once per
timepoint. Copies with the same QTL are identical predictors and split their
PIP, but they fall in the same credible set, so a gene's `combined_pip` (all its
parts and timepoints, `combine_gene_pips()` with `by = "type"`) adds them back.

## Parameters

```{r joint_params}
w <- jp[group != "SNP"][, snp_prior := jp[group == "SNP", prior]]
knitr::kable(w[, .(group, group_size=fmt(group_size), `group_prior (splicing)`=sprintf("%.4f", prior), `group_prior (SNP)`=sprintf("%.5f", snp_prior),
  group_prior_var=sprintf("%.1f", prior_var), `log_enrichment (log_enrichment_se)`=sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", log_enrichment, log_enrichment_se),
  enrichment_pval=fp(enrichment_pval), group_pve=sprintf("%.4f", pve), total_pve=sprintf("%.3f", total_pve),
  prop_heritability=sprintf("%.4f", prop_heritability))], align="lrrrrrrrrr")
```

**1 hr** (ours): its `group_prior` is `r sprintf("%.0e", gp("1hr")$prior)`, so its
`log_enrichment` is very negative and its standard error meaningless. In a joint
run the timepoints compete for the same GWAS signal, and the 1 hr traits explain
nothing beyond the 0 and 6 hr traits. Identical traits alone don't explain it:
about 20% of 1 hr traits are copies of a 0 or 6 hr trait, as with the `cis`
label alone, where 1 hr kept a `log_enrichment` of 3.53.

## Gene-level PIPs

Genes with `combined_pip` of at least 0.5.

```{r joint_genes}
old_pip <- function(gn) vapply(gn, function(x) { v <- cmp[gene_name == x, gene_pip_isolaser]; if (length(v)) v else NA_real_ }, 0)
d <- jg[gene_pip >= 0.5][order(-gene_pip)]
knitr::kable(d[, .(gene_name, combined_pip=sprintf("%.2f", gene_pip), `0hr_pip`=cell(pip_0hr), `1hr_pip`=cell(pip_1hr), `6hr_pip`=cell(pip_6hr),
  `isoLASER only (earlier page)`=cell(old_pip(gene_name)), Traits=n_traits, `Top part`=top_part, Timepoint=tpl(top_tp),
  `susie_pip (top part)`=sprintf("%.2f", top_part_pip), z=sprintf("%.1f", z), `QTL (UKB ID)`=ukb_id, `&Delta;PSI`=sprintf("%+.3f", dpsi),
  `Permutation p`=fp(qtl_p))], escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrrrlllrlrr")
```

- **combined_pip:** over all of the gene's parts and timepoints (`by = "type"`).
- **0hr_pip, 1hr_pip, 6hr_pip:** `combine_gene_pips()` with `by = "context"`, the
  gene's PIP from that timepoint's traits only; "&ndash;" means none of its traits
  at that timepoint is in a fine-mapped region.
- **isoLASER only (earlier page):** the gene's `combined_pip` in the joint run with
  the `cis` label alone; "&ndash;" means not in a fine-mapped region there.
- **Traits:** the gene's part &times; timepoint traits in fine-mapped regions.
- **Top part, Timepoint, susie_pip (top part), z, QTL, ΔPSI, permutation p:** the
  trait with the largest `susie_pip`, its z-score and its isoLASER association.

## Plausibility of the genes at combined_pip 0.8

**NDRG4, SF3B1 and MYT1L sit at genome-wide significant SCZ loci, and LY6H has
the strongest splicing effect.** YWHAE has a sub-threshold signal here but a PGC3
SCZ association 3 kb from its SNP. GOPC, MRPL43, CNPPD1 and PIGF are at loci
without a genome-wide significant SNP within 250 kb; their PIP rests on the high
6 hr enrichment. Biological plausibility of a gene and support for its particular
splicing association are assessed separately below.

```{r joint_plausibility, results='asis'}
ev <- fread(file.path(A, "joint_gene_evidence.tsv"), na.strings=c("", "NA"))
verdict <- c(NDRG4="Strong candidate; sizable effects, but low read counts",
  SF3B1="Strong SCZ locus and GTEx cTWAS support; moderate splicing effect at 0 hr",
  MYT1L="Strong neuronal and SCZ support; modest splicing effect",
  LY6H="Strong mechanistic candidate and splicing evidence; suggestive GWAS signal",
  YWHAE="Sub-threshold here, but a PGC3 SCZ association 3 kb away; small splicing effect",
  GOPC="Exploratory; no genome-wide significant SNP within 250 kb",
  MRPL43="Exploratory; sub-threshold locus, but the SNP is a GTEx brain sQTL",
  CNPPD1="Exploratory; low coverage and weak permutation evidence",
  PIGF="Neurodevelopmental relevance; limited SCZ-specific support")
stopifnot(setequal(unique(ev$gene_name), j8), setequal(names(verdict), j8))
ref <- function(author, pmid, doi) sprintf('%s (<a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/%s/">PMID %s</a>; <a href="https://doi.org/%s">paper</a>)', author, pmid, pmid, doi)
# literature notes as on the earlier page; YWHAE, GOPC and MRPL43 are new here and their literature was not reviewed
support <- c(
  NDRG4=paste0("GWAS Catalog links rs42945 to the SCZ association results of ", ref("Pardi&ntilde;as 2018", "29483656", "10.1038/s41588-018-0059-2"), "; the SNP and NDRG4 are not named in the main article. ", ref("Collado-Torres 2019", "31174959", "10.1016/j.neuron.2019.05.013"), " explicitly identifies rs42945 as a SCZ risk SNP and reports associations with NDRG4 RNA expression features in hippocampus (Supplementary Fig. S43A-B). This supports NDRG4 regulation, but does not establish replication of the same splicing event. Ndrg4-deficient mice have reduced cortical BDNF and impaired spatial learning: ", ref("Yamamoto 2011", "21636852", "10.1074/jbc.M111.256446"), "."),
  MYT1L=paste0("Maintains neuronal identity: ", ref("Mall 2017", "28379941", "10.1038/nature21722"), ". Prioritized by PGC3 SCZ fine-mapping: ", ref("Trubetskoy 2022", "35396580", "10.1038/s41586-022-04434-5"), "."),
  SF3B1=paste0("Core spliceosome component. Independent SCZ regulatory evidence and inclusion in a human-neuron perturbation study: ", ref("Deans et al. 2026", "41519853", "10.1038/s41467-025-67959-z"), "."),
  LY6H=paste0("Regulates alpha7 nicotinic receptor trafficking and nicotine-induced potentiation of glutamatergic signaling: ", ref("Puddifoot 2015", "25716842", "10.1523/JNEUROSCI.3630-14.2015"), ". No genome-wide significant SNP within 250 kb in this GWAS; this does not establish novelty."),
  CNPPD1=paste0("Limited neuronal functional evidence. The catalog association 7 kb away comes from a multi-trait psychiatric analysis, not independent SCZ-only confirmation: ", ref("Wu 2020", "32606422", "10.1038/s41398-020-00902-6"), "."),
  PIGF=paste0("GPI-anchor biosynthesis. Rare biallelic variants were reported in a syndrome with intellectual disability and seizures: ", ref("Salian 2021", "33386993", "10.1007/s00439-020-02251-2"), ". This is neurodevelopmental evidence, not common-variant SCZ replication."),
  YWHAE="Literature not reviewed (new here).", GOPC="Literature not reviewed (new here).", MRPL43="Literature not reviewed (new here).")
br <- function(x) paste(x, collapse="<br>")
numrange <- function(x, formatter) {
  z <- formatter(range(x))
  if (z[1] == z[2]) z[1] else paste(z, collapse=" to ")
}
pip_cell <- function(gn) {
  row <- jg[gene_name == gn]
  br(c(sprintf("<strong>Overall %.3f</strong>", row$gene_pip), vapply(TPS, function(t) {
    n <- jtr[gene_name == gn & context == t, uniqueN(molecular_id)]
    p <- row[[paste0("pip_", t)]]
    if (is.na(p)) paste0(tpl(t), ": &ndash;") else sprintf("%s: %.3f (%d %s)", tpl(t), p, n, ifelse(n == 1, "part", "parts"))
  }, "")))
}
effect_cell <- function(gn) {
  z <- jtr[gene_name == gn & susie_pip >= 0.05]
  z <- z[order(match(context, TPS))]
  br(z[, .(text=sprintf("%s, %s: &Delta;PSI %s; p %s; %s reads", tpl(context[1]), ukb_id[1],
    numrange(dpsi, function(x) sprintf("%+.3f", x)), numrange(qtl_p, fp), numrange(het_cov, fmt))),
    by=.(context, ukb_id)]$text)
}
support_cell <- function(gn) {
  e <- ev[gene_name == gn][1]
  extra <- character()
  if (gn %in% c("YWHAE", "GOPC", "MRPL43") && !is.na(e$catalog_nearest))
    extra <- c(extra, sprintf("Nearest GWAS Catalog SCZ association (p &le; 5e-8): %s, %d kb from the SNP.", e$catalog_nearest, abs(e$catalog_nearest_kb)))
  if (e$gtex_sqtl_tissues > 0) extra <- c(extra, sprintf("The selected SNP is a GTEx sQTL for this gene in %d of 13 brain tissues (minimum p %s).", e$gtex_sqtl_tissues, fp(e$gtex_sqtl_min_p)))
  if (!is.na(e$gtex_ctwas_pip) && e$gtex_ctwas_pip >= 0.1) extra <- c(extra, sprintf("GTEx cerebellum eQTL + sQTL cTWAS gene PIP: %.2f.", e$gtex_ctwas_pip))
  br(c(support[[gn]], extra))
}
ord <- c("NDRG4", "SF3B1", "MYT1L", "LY6H", "YWHAE", "GOPC", "MRPL43", "CNPPD1", "PIGF")
stopifnot(setequal(ord, j8))
pt <- rbindlist(lapply(ord, function(gn) {
  e <- ev[gene_name == gn][1]
  data.table(Gene=gn, `Joint combined PIP: overall and by timepoint`=pip_cell(gn),
    `Allelic splicing: signed effect, permutation p, reads`=effect_cell(gn),
    `SCZ GWAS p at selected SNP`=paste0(e$qtl_snp, "<br>", fp(e$gwas_p)),
    `Best GWAS p within 250 kb`=fp(e$nearby_min_p),
    `Other evidence`=support_cell(gn), Plausibility=verdict[[gn]])
}))
cat('<div style="overflow-x:auto;">\n')
cat(knitr::kable(pt, format="html", escape=FALSE, row.names=FALSE), sep="\n")
cat('\n</div>\n')
```

- **PIP and part counts:** include all fine-mapped predictors for the gene.
  A dash means no fine-mapped predictor at that timepoint. The calculation uses
  `combine_gene_pips(method="combine_cs", filter_cs=FALSE)`, with `by="context"`
  for each timepoint and `by="type"` for the overall splicing PIP.
- **Splicing effects:** summarize parts with individual predictor PIP at least
  0.05, grouped by timepoint and QTL SNP. With the filter, no part has 2,371 or
  more reads.
- **Delta PSI:** ALT inclusion minus REF inclusion; +0.250 means +25 percentage
  points. **Permutation p** is unadjusted. **Reads** are pooled informative reads
  from the heterozygous donors. Ranges summarize several parts, not confidence
  intervals; low counts can produce uncertain effect estimates.
- **Selected SNP:** the QTL of the part with the largest predictor PIP. The GWAS
  columns refer to that SNP and its surrounding 250 kb on either side in the SCZ
  GWAS used here (`ieu-b-5102`). Genome-wide significance is p < 5e-8.
- **GWAS Catalog** (new genes only): the nearest association whose mapped trait
  contains "schizophrenia" with p &le; 5e-8, within 500 kb (GRCh38). It can come
  from a larger GWAS than the one used here.
- **GTEx support:** a significant SNP-intron association for the same SNP and
  gene in GTEx v8 brain tissues. It need not measure the same exonic part, so it
  is **not automatically replication of the specific splicing event**. No match
  in these significant-pair files does not establish absence of an effect.
- **Interpretation:** high cTWAS PIP supports a predictor under the fitted model;
  it does not prove that the particular splicing event mediates SCZ risk. With
  one-SNP predictors, separation from the SNP depends strongly on the model's
  priors. The high 6 hr enrichment can favor predictors even at suggestive loci.

  `6hr_pip`=round(pip_6hr, 3), Traits=n_traits, `Top part`=top_part, Timepoint=tpl(top_tp), `susie_pip (top part)`=round(top_part_pip, 3),
  z=round(z, 2), QTL=ukb_id, dPSI=round(dpsi, 3), `Permutation p`=signif(qtl_p, 2))][order(-combined_pip)]), rownames=FALSE, filter="top",
